questions.question: If a machine does 500 J of work in 4 seconds, what is its power output?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**125 watt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.
 
• The formula to calculate power is **Power = Work / Time**.
 
• In this case, the work done is 500 joules and the time taken is 4 seconds.
 
• Using the formula, the power output is **500 J / 4 s = 125 watts**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joule (J)**: The SI unit of work or energy. One joule is the amount of work done when a force of one newton displaces an object by one meter in the direction of the force.
 
• **Watt (W)**: The SI unit of power. One watt is equal to one joule per second.
 
• **Energy**: The capacity to do work. It can exist in various forms such as kinetic, potential, thermal, electrical, chemical, and nuclear energy.
 
• **SI Units**: The International System of Units (SI) is the modern form of the metric system and the world's most widely used system of measurement.

questions.question: A book is lying on a table and Rahul moves the book in the direction of the force for some distance D. The work done by the force is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**positive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The work done by a force is defined as the product of the force and the displacement in the direction of the force.
 
• In this scenario, since Rahul moves the book in the direction of the applied force, the displacement is in the same direction as the force.
 
• When the force and displacement are in the same direction, the work done is positive.
 
• The formula for work done (W) is given by W = F × D × cos(θ), where θ is the angle between the force and the displacement. Here, θ = 0 degrees, and cos(0) = 1.
 
• Thus, W = F × D × 1 = F × D, which is a positive value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work**

 
 
• In physics, work is defined as the energy transferred to or from an object via the application of force along a displacement.
 
• It is a scalar quantity and is measured in Joules (J).
 
• The concept of work is closely related to energy, which is the capacity to do work.
 
 
 
• **Force**
 
 
• Force is any interaction that, when unopposed, will change the motion of an object.
 
• It is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.
 
• It is measured in Newtons (N).
 
 
 
• **Displacement**
 
 
• Displacement is the vector quantity that defines the distance and direction between the initial and final positions of an object.
 
• It is distinct from distance, which is a scalar quantity and does not consider direction.
 
 
 
• **Positive Work**
 
 
• Positive work occurs when the force applied on an object and the displacement of the object are in the same direction.
 
• Examples include lifting a book upwards or pushing a box forward.

questions.question: If 7 N force is applied on a brick and it moves through 5 m, then what will be the work done?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**35 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Work is calculated using the formula: **Work = Force × Displacement × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between the force and displacement.
 
• Here, the force applied is **7 N**, and the displacement is **5 m**.
 
• If the force and displacement are in the same direction, cos(θ) = cos(0°) = 1.
 
• Thus, Work = 7 × 5 × 1 = **35 J**.
 
• The unit of work in the SI system is the **joule (J)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work:**

 
 
• Work is done when a force is applied to an object, and the object moves in the direction of the force.
 
• It is a scalar quantity, meaning it has magnitude but no direction.
 
• The formula for work (W) is **W = F × d × cos(θ)**, where:
 
 
• F = Force applied (N)
 
• d = Displacement (m)
 
• θ = Angle between the force and displacement
 
 
 
 
 
• **Joule:**
 
 
• The joule (J) is the SI unit of work and energy.
 
• **1 joule is equivalent to 1 newton-meter (N·m)**.
 
• It represents the work done when a force of 1 newton displaces an object by 1 meter in the direction of the force.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Work:**
 
 
• The magnitude of the force applied.
 
• The displacement caused by the force.
 
• The angle between the force and the displacement.
 
 
 
• **Work in Different Systems:**
 
 
• In the CGS system, the unit of work is the erg.
 
• **1 erg = 10⁻⁷ joules.**

questions.question: If k is the spring’s force constant and x is the displacement from its undeformed position of a spring, then the potential energy (V) of the spring is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**V = kx² / 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The potential energy (V) stored in a spring is given by the formula **V = (1/2)kx²**, where **k** is the spring constant and **x** is the displacement from the spring's equilibrium position.
 
• This formula is derived from Hooke's Law, which states that the force exerted by a spring is proportional to its displacement: **F = -kx**.
 
• The potential energy corresponds to the work done in deforming the spring, which is equivalent to the area under the force-displacement curve (a triangle).
 
• The spring constant (**k**) represents the stiffness of the spring and is measured in **Newton/meter (N/m)**.
 
• The displacement (**x**) is the distance the spring is stretched or compressed from its natural (undeformed) position, measured in meters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hooke's Law:**

 
 
• Hooke's Law states that the force exerted by a spring is directly proportional to its displacement: **F = -kx**.
 
• The negative sign indicates that the spring force is restorative, meaning it acts in the opposite direction of displacement.
 
 
 
• **Elastic Potential Energy:**
 
 
• Elastic potential energy is the energy stored in elastic materials, such as springs, when they are stretched or compressed.
 
• This energy is released when the material returns to its equilibrium state.
 
 
 
• **Spring Constant (k):**
 
 
• The spring constant is a measure of the stiffness of the spring.
 
• A higher value of **k** indicates a stiffer spring, which requires more force to produce the same displacement.
 
 
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:**
 
 
• The work done on the spring to compress or stretch it is stored as potential energy.
 
• This theorem is the foundation for deriving the formula for the spring's potential energy.

__
 
• The sum of the kinetic and potential energy of an object is known as the** Total Mechanical Energy.**
 
• **Kinetic Energy** is the energy that an **object possesses due to its motion**.
 
• **Potential Energy** is the energy stored in an object due to its** position or configuration**.
 
• The principle of conservation of mechanical energy states that if only conservative forces are acting, the total mechanical energy of a system remains constant.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Total Mechanical Energy
 This is the correct answer. It represents the sum of an object's kinetic and potential energy.
 
 

 Total Frictional Energy
 Frictional energy refers to the energy lost due to friction. It is not related to the sum of kinetic and potential energy.
 
 

 Total Heat Energy
 Heat energy is the result of the movement of tiny particles called atoms, molecules or ions in solids, liquids, and gases. It is not the sum of kinetic and potential energy.
 
 

 Total Potential Energy
 Potential energy is just one part of the total mechanical energy, not the sum of kinetic and potential energy.

questions.question: An object is displaced horizontally because of the applied force. What is revealed by this action?

options.text: The force decreases the mass of the object.
The force increases the mass of the object.
The force increases the inertia of the object.
Work is done by the force.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Work is done by the force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a force causes displacement of an object in the direction of the applied force, **work is done** on the object.
 
• Work is defined as the product of the force applied and the displacement of the object in the direction of the force: **W = F × d**.
 
• The SI unit of work is the **joule (J)**, which is equivalent to one newton-meter.
 
• This concept is fundamental in physics and explains how energy is transferred from one object to another through force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force**

 
 
• A force is any interaction that, when unopposed, will change the motion of an object.
 
• Forces can cause objects to accelerate, decelerate, remain in place, or change shape.
 
• The SI unit of force is the newton (N).
 
 
 
• **Energy**
 
 
• Energy is the capacity to do work.
 
• It exists in various forms such as kinetic, potential, thermal, electrical, chemical, and nuclear energy.
 
• Energy can be transformed from one form to another but cannot be created or destroyed (law of conservation of energy).
 
 
 
• **Displacement**
 
 
• Displacement is a vector quantity that refers to the change in position of an object.
 
• It has both magnitude and direction.
 
• Displacement is different from distance, which is a scalar quantity representing the total path length covered.
 
 
 
• **Inertia**
 
 
• Inertia is the resistance of any physical object to a change in its state of motion or rest.
 
• It is directly related to the mass of the object.
 
• An object with greater mass has more inertia.

questions.question: A girl of weight 440 N climbs up a rope through a height of 7 m in 20 s. The power expended by the girl is:
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• Power is defined as the rate of doing work.
 
• This unit of power is Watt (W)
 
• If a device does a work (W) in time (t), then its power (P) is given by the formula,
 
 
• P = frac Wt
 
 
 
• Work is defined as when the force acting on a body displaces the body in its direction.
 
• We can calculate work (W) using the formula W = F × s 
 
• where, F is the force applied, and s is the displacement caused by the force along its direction.

**Calculation:**__

Given, weight, F = 440 N, height, s = 7 m, Time, t = 20 s

Work, W = 440 × 7 

Now, power P = frac Wt 

Rightarrow P = frac {440 times 7}{20} 

P = 154 W

questions.question: An object A with a mass m and velocity v has a kinetic energy of 100 J. Then the kinetic energy of an object B with a mass of 2 m and velocity v is:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**200 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **kinetic energy** (K.E.) of an object is given by the formula, KE=(1)/(2)mv² where **m** is the mass and **v** is the velocity of the object.
 
• Given: Object A has a kinetic energy of **100 J** with mass **m** and velocity **v**.
 
• The kinetic energy of object A is calculated as KE_A=(1)/(2)mv²=100J
 
• For object B, the mass is **2m** and the velocity remains **v**.
 
• Substitute these values into the kinetic energy formula for object B: KE_B=(1)/(2)×2mtimes v²=2KE_A
 
• Thus, KE_B=2×100=200J.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **200 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy**__

 __
 
• **Kinetic energy** is the energy that an object possesses due to its motion.
 
• It is directly proportional to the **mass** of the object and the square of its **velocity**.
 
• The standard unit for measuring kinetic energy is the **Joule (J)**.
 
 
 
• **Mass and Velocity**__
 
 
• In the given problem, the mass **m** and velocity **v** are crucial factors that determine the kinetic energy.
 
• Doubling the **mass** while keeping the velocity constant doubles the kinetic energy.

questions.question: When a horse pulls a cart on a level road, the work done is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Positive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Positive work done means that force is parallel to displacement.**
 
• When a horse pulls a cart, it gives force in the forwarding direction.
 
 
• If the force is enough to displace the cart, the cart will displace in the same direction as the exerted force by the horse. 
 
• So the **work done is positive.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Negative work done means that force is opposite to displacement**.

 
 
• Example: when a positive charge is moved towards another positive charge.
 
 
 
• **If the force is perpendicular to the displacement and if either the force or the displacement is zero, work done will be zero**.
 
 
• Example: when a coolie travels on a platform with a load on his head.

__
 
• **As the particle goes upward**, its velocity decreases and height increases. 

 
 
• **Therefore kinetic energy diminishes as it goes up and gets converted into potential energy**__.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When a body is thrown vertically **upwards**, at the highest point the **velocity is zero because the acceleration due to gravitational force is acting downward continuously **and that is the reason for velocity being zero at the highest point, hence velocity is zero because of the acceleration.

 
 
• At the starting of throwing off the body's initial velocity is zero and its **Potential energy is minimum**.
 
• After throwing the body vertically upward its kinetic energy goes on decreasing while potential energy increases.
 
• At the highest point, kinetic energy becomes zero and potential energy is maximum and again the same cycle repeats.
